name: George Wythe House

dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox and the Library's item both print 1754; the DHR entry says 'erected ca. 1750 by the builder Richard Taliaferro, who most likely was its designer'. Recorded as the item states it, with the DHR's date noted.

refs.title: George Wythe House, 101 Palace Green Street, Williamsburg, Independent City, VA
refs.note: The item's note line reads 'Survey number: HABS VA-1009; Building/structure dates: 1754 Initial Construction; National Register of Historic Places NRIS Number: 70000866'; call number HABS VA,48-WIL,16-, 10 sheets. Wikipedia's external-links line gives '10 measured drawings'. The data PDF fetched is a one-line cover for the reduced drawings ('Wythe, George, House HABS VA-1009 ... REDUCED DRAWINGS'), so there is no written data and this record carries no survey block.

note: Written 4 Sep 2026 from the WP-11.1 research pass; a new exemplar on georgian-colonial-american. The DHR calls it the house that has 'spawned so many imitations', and its ten HABS sheets are the reason it is here: a plain five-bay brick double pile a generator can be held against, with no written data to quote.
